It appears that **no country** meets all four criteria simultaneously in 2021. The primary issue is that these two criteria overlap very little geographically. Countries meeting the low life expectancy criterion typically have smoking rates well below 10-15%, while countries with smoking rates above 30% generally have life expectancies above 70 years.

**Obesity (>10%) and NCD deaths (>25%):**
These two criteria are actually met by almost all countries globally, so they don't significantly narrow the selection. Nearly every nation has adult obesity rates exceeding 10%, and the probability of dying from NCDs before age 70 exceeds 25% worldwide.

### Conclusion:

It appears that **no country** meets all four criteria simultaneously in 2021. The geographic and demographic patterns create an intersection that's likely empty or contains at most one or two outlier countries that require direct database verification using WHO Global Health Estimates or Our World in Data dashboards for precise confirmation.
